$comment: Reference photographs shown alongside the model. These are visual reference ONLY: SOURCE-REGISTER.md marks SRC-002 visual-only, and test STT-017 fails the build if any of them is ever cited by a control dimension. Captions are transcribed from the HAER index to photographs (ny1263cap.pdf), not paraphrased.

archive.title: Historic American Engineering Record, Williamsburg Bridge, HAER No. NY-128
archive.repository: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division
archive.rights: Public domain. Works of the United States Government; no known restrictions on publication.

foundVia.title: historic-structures.com — The Historic Williamsburg Bridge in NYC
foundVia.note: This page surfaced the photographs and carries many more. The images here were retrieved from the Library of Congress originals at full resolution rather than copied from it.

photos.caption: Williamsburg Bridge, looking northwest, Manhattan tower
photos.compare: The clearest view of what this model calls the Manhattan tower: two legs on two separate masonry piers, the upper legs slanted inward, and the deck passing between them.

photos.caption: Williamsburg Bridge from Brooklyn to Manhattan, bridge in perspective
photos.compare: Whole structure end to end. The side span and its intermediate supports are visible on the left — the geometry behind OQ-001 and OQ-003, both still open.

photos.caption: Williamsburg Bridge over the East River looking south towards Brooklyn on the left and Manhattan on the right
photos.compare: The main span in elevation, with the cable profile against the sky. The model's cable sag is a placeholder (CTL-102) and this photograph cannot fix it — no scale, no camera.

photos.caption: Williamsburg Bridge, roadway and Manhattan skyline
photos.compare: Deck level. The five-section division the model uses is sourced only at its outermost width; the interior split is reasoned (OQ-007).

photos.caption: Williamsburg Bridge from Williamsburg community looking southwest towards Manhattan
photos.compare: The Brooklyn approach running inland, at the 3 percent grade of CTL-036.

photos.caption: View from Manhattan with Brooklyn in right background
photos.compare: Before the 1980s and 1990s reconstruction, which replaced both roadways with orthotropic decks.
